title: Runtime: TP watchdog timeout + safe abort/drain path for stalled steps
author: Noah Patel
release_notes: - Adds feature-flagged TP watchdog to detect stalled decode/prefill steps and trigger a controlled abort. - On stall, replica enters draining state, rejects new work, and returns actionable error code to the API layer instead of hanging. - Exposes structured stall events for SRE automation hooks (drain/replace) and dashboards.
description: Context: We have recurring Sev1/Sev2s where a TP replica silently stalls (most commonly during decode under mixed prefill/decode load). Today that manifests as requests hanging until upstream timeouts, with the replica continuing to accept work and compounding the blast radius. This PR introduces a feature-flagged watchdog that detects “no forward progress” in TP execution and triggers a controlled abort + replica drain. Goal is to fail fast, drain safely, and prevent GPU wedging / queue pileups while we continue to harden scheduler + NCCL ordering. What this PR does: (1) Adds a TP step watchdog that monitors progress at two levels: per-request “decode iteration progress” and per-rank “collective step counter” (fed by existing TP step bookkeeping; see ENG-4823/PR-21834 for richer metrics). The watchdog is implemented as a lightweight timer in the TP execution loop with a monotonic clock and is careful to avoid extra CUDA synchronizations in the healthy path. (2) Defines stall semantics and thresholds: a stall is declared when no progress is observed for longer than runtime.tp_watchdog.timeout_ms (default conservative; overridden via config by model class). We also support separate timeouts for prefill vs decode because long prefill can legitimately exceed decode thresholds on long-context prompts. (3) Adds safe abort behavior: on stall, we mark the replica “draining”, stop admitting new requests, and terminate in-flight TP work with a controlled error path. We intentionally do not attempt to recover the in-process TP state. Instead, we surface a structured RuntimeError with code TP_STALL_ABORTED, attach context (replica_id, tp_group_size, model_id, phase, last_progress_ms, pending_collectives), and rely on orchestrator/SRE automation to replace the replica. (4) Integrates SRE mitigation hooks: emits a drain event (rate-limited/deduped per replica) and a “stall detected” marker so SRE can tie alerts to automated drain/replace actions. This aligns with the on-call mitigation flow used in the 2025-02-17 incident (SUP-48321). (5) Feature flag + rollout: gated behind runtime.tp_watchdog.enabled (default off). Also supports runtime.tp_watchdog.drain_on_stall (default on when enabled) to allow dry-run in dev/perf environments where we only log. Implementation notes: - Watchdog avoids adding additional stream syncs; we only read host-side progress counters updated at known safe points. - Abort path cancels request futures, transitions scheduler to “reject new”, and triggers replica drain callback. - For streaming requests, we send a terminal error frame and close the stream to avoid client hangs. - Includes unit tests for stall detection and integration tests using a simulated “stalled step” hook (fault injection) rather than requiring real NCCL deadlocks in CI. Rollout/operational guidance: - Enable first in perf-canary with drain_on_stall=false to validate signal quality (no false positives). - Then enable drain_on_stall=true for a small Dedicated canary slice with extended logging (INT-2219) and strict rollback criteria (any increase in abort rate without correlated timeout reduction). - If we see false positives, raise per-model thresholds and/or narrow stall detection to decode-only while we refine progress accounting. Related: ENG-4826 (this change), ENG-4821 umbrella, PR-21834 (TP heartbeat/metrics), PR-21912 (error surfacing improvements; follow-up), PR-21875 (load-shed on stall signal; follow-up).

review_summary: Key review points: (1) SRE requested clear rollout toggles and a dry-run mode to measure false positives; added runtime.tp_watchdog.drain_on_stall and improved structured logging fields for correlation. (2) Scheduling review requested that drain happens before we unblock scheduler queues to prevent additional work being enqueued; reordered state transitions and added a guard in replica admission control. (3) Kernel review requested that abort path never calls blocking CUDA syncs; removed an early cudaDeviceSynchronize() from the first draft and replaced with non-blocking cancellation + replica drain. (4) Streaming review requested deterministic termination behavior for client disconnect vs server abort; added explicit terminal error frame and ensured we close streams after sending it. (5) Tests: reviewers asked for fault-injection coverage to avoid relying on real NCCL deadlocks; added a simulated ‘stall hook’ and time-control utilities to make the watchdog deterministic in unit tests. Approvals: Hiro Tanaka, Sofia Ivanova, Rafael Mendes; SRE sign-off conditional on canary flag default off and documented rollback criteria (included in description).
conversation: Hiro Tanaka: Please confirm this doesn’t introduce implicit sync in the hot path. Sampling counters is fine; any cudaEventQuery or stream sync needs to be gated/avoided. Noah Patel: Agreed. Healthy path only reads host-side counters updated after existing boundary points; no new CUDA API calls in the steady-state loop. The only heavy action is in the stall handler and even there we avoid device-wide sync; we drain and let the supervisor recycle the replica. Sofia Ivanova: Drain ordering matters. If the scheduler continues to admit requests while the watchdog is firing we’ll amplify the queue. Can we flip admission off before we begin aborting inflight work? Noah Patel: Updated: on stall we atomically set replica_state=Draining, then scheduler admission checks reject new work. Inflight requests are then failed with TP_STALL_ABORTED and the drain hook is invoked. Rafael Mendes: Need dry-run mode and explicit config keys for canary. Also please add a structured field for phase (prefill/decode) and last_progress_ms. Noah Patel: Added runtime.tp_watchdog.enabled and runtime.tp_watchdog.drain_on_stall. Also added structured log payload: stall_phase, last_progress_ms, tp_group_size, pending_collectives. Aisha Bello: Alerting will key off the stall event. Please ensure it is rate-limited per replica so we don’t page storm during a single wedge. Noah Patel: Added dedupe (one stall event per replica per drain interval) and a counter metric for aggregate visibility; detailed alert tuning will be in observability PR. Tomáš Novák: Please link the on-call runbook section for immediate mitigations and include rollback guidance (disable flag). Noah Patel: Added docs pointer + explicit rollback: toggle runtime.tp_watchdog.enabled=false and restart runtime pods; no data migration needed.
merge_outcome: Merged to main via squash. Backport requested to release/1.19 after 48h canary signal validation.
